review_standard: Editorially reviewed public-source case summaries. All customer statements are attributed to their reporting source; bank involvement is not a finding of fault. Cases are not an exhaustive list. Investigation sequences restate the attributed case summary; analyst questions are research prompts, not findings.

incidents.title: Tangerine customer reports C$7,200 courier bank-impersonation scam
incidents.location_role: reported customer city, not incident coordinates
incidents.fraud_type: Bank impersonation / debit card collection scam
incidents.recovery_status: Customer reported a partial settlement, without full reimbursement
incidents.source_name: CBC Marketplace story (reproduced by Today in Canada)
incidents.summary: A Toronto customer reported a caller impersonating Tangerine's fraud team who arranged collection of a debit card by courier. Media coverage reports a C$7,200 loss and a later partial settlement; the fraud occurred months before publication.
incidents.consulting_theme: Spoofed bank calls, scam interventions, courier-card fraud, reimbursement and claims handling
incidents.disclaimer: A customer-reported loss and reimbursement dispute, not an adjudicated finding of wrongdoing by Tangerine. Secondary reproduction of CBC reporting.

stages: A customer reported receiving a call from someone claiming to represent Tangerine's fraud team.
The caller arranged for a courier to collect a debit card.
Coverage described a partial settlement, rather than full reimbursement.
questions: What communications and card-collection steps does the publication actually establish?
What reimbursement or recovery outcome is supported by the reporting?
Which controls could interrupt courier-assisted bank impersonation, without assuming this bank was at fault?

incidents.title: Vancouver employee loses C$34,000 to bank impersonation
incidents.incident_period: Before October 22, 2026; exact day not stated
incidents.summary: Vancouver police described a spoofed caller impersonating a bank representative. A victim was persuaded to provide information enabling withdrawals from two accounts.
incidents.consulting_theme: Bank impersonation, credential compromise, account access and customer education
incidents.disclaimer: The police notice does not name the bank. No bank misconduct is implied.

stages: Vancouver police described a caller impersonating a bank representative.
Police reported that the victim was persuaded to provide information.
The information reportedly enabled withdrawals from two accounts.
The police release described a C$34,000 loss.
questions: What exact customer information was requested, and what is not specified in the police release?
Which access and payment steps are confirmed versus unknown?
What intervention points might address spoofed-bank contact and account access?

incidents.title: B.C. customer reports C$450,000 deepfake investment scam
incidents.recovery_status: Reported as not reimbursed at publication
incidents.source_name: Yahoo Finance (reporting on CBC Go Public)
incidents.summary: A customer reported losing money over months after seeing a deepfake investment promotion. The article describes payments made through a TD account and disputes about protective interventions.
incidents.consulting_theme: Scam intervention, vulnerability identification, unusual transfer behavior
incidents.disclaimer: This case is a reported customer loss, not a regulatory finding against TD.

stages: A customer reported encountering a deepfake investment promotion.
The report describes payments through a TD account over a period spanning May 2025 to February 2026.
The customer reported an approximately C$450,000 loss.
The coverage describes disagreement about protective interventions; reimbursement was not reported at publication.
questions: Which investment-promotion claims are confirmed by sources, and which remain customer allegations?
What payment sequence and time gaps are independently documented?
What indicators, if any, could distinguish coercive scam activity from legitimate investing?

incidents.title: Ontario customer reports C$35,000 unauthorized credit line
incidents.location_role: reported customer residence; credit line allegedly opened in Milton
incidents.summary: Customer said an unauthorized credit line was created at a Milton branch and exhausted; the article reported that the bank later refunded the amount.
incidents.consulting_theme: Identity verification, branch authentication, credit account opening
incidents.disclaimer: Unauthorized credit exposure is not necessarily a realized loss borne by the bank.

stages: The customer reported that a credit line was opened without authorization.
Coverage identified a Milton branch in connection with the reported opening.
The reported unauthorized credit exposure was C$35,000.
The article stated that the amount was later refunded.
questions: What evidence establishes the credit-opening channel and disputed identity-verification steps?
How should unauthorized credit exposure be distinguished from final victim loss?
Which outcome details and dates are corroborated by the original reporting?

incidents.title: C$3.5 million recovered after Québec payment-redirection fraud
incidents.location_role: victim province; no sufficiently precise incident location
incidents.recovery_status: C$3.5 million recovered according to CAFC
incidents.summary: CAFC reported working with a financial institution to recover funds after a Québec business followed fraudulent payment instructions. The amount is recovered funds, not a bank loss.
incidents.consulting_theme: Payment instruction change, beneficiary validation, fraud recall and intervention
incidents.disclaimer: C$3.5 million is a reported recovery amount, not a victim net loss and not a penalty.

stages: A Québec business reportedly followed fraudulent payment instructions.
CAFC reported coordinating with a financial institution to recover the funds.
Approximately C$3.5 million was recovered, according to CAFC.
questions: Which payment-instruction changes are described in the government release?
What roles did the reporting entity and assisting financial institution have?
What can and cannot be inferred from a recovered amount?

incidents.title: Nanaimo resident reports C$24,000 bank impersonation loss
incidents.incident_period: Before February 24, 2026; exact day not stated
incidents.summary: RCMP described a local resident receiving calls and messages appearing to come from RBC; the victim reportedly gave personal details to scammers who accessed accounts.
incidents.consulting_theme: Spoofed communications, account takeover, high-risk transaction monitoring
incidents.disclaimer: RBC is the impersonated institution, not an accused party.

stages: RCMP described calls and messages that appeared to come from RBC.
The resident reportedly shared personal information with the callers.
Scammers reportedly gained access to accounts.
A loss of approximately C$24,000 was reported.
questions: Which delivery channels were actually used by the impersonators?
What account-access steps were verified versus inferred?
How does identifying RBC as impersonated differ from alleging misconduct by RBC?
